chapter: Telephone reels: blues and Bessie Smith
title: Bessie Smith in the studio and Edith Wilson's lesser recognition
summary: Rasch asks about Handy and Bessie Smith's meticulousness; Johnson says Smith liked things just so, and that recognition depended on era.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Uh-huh. One of the books I was reading was -- this young man was asked -- this was maybe in the '50s. And he was asked -- '50s or maybe even more than that -- he was asked how he got into blues. Now, I guess this happened maybe in the late '50s. And he said -- or maybe it was in the early '60s.
He said, "When I was 13, my mother bought me a Bessie Smith album and said, 'Here, get off that rock and roll stuff.'"
That's adorable. That's right. I would say that you -- you've heard Handy play, haven't you, W. C. Handy play?
No? You haven't heard a record of him playing or anything at all?

No, I've heard his records, but -- I mean I've heard the 'St. Louis Blues', but people say -- some people say he didn't write it, but just spread it. (Inaudible). By the way, J. C., let me know if you're getting a little tired. Okay? (Inaudible) They say that Bessie Smith took more care in her performances than a lot of artists, you know, that she was very --
-- thorough, very meticulous, and I wondered if you had any instances like when she taped 'Empty Bed Blues' or anything else that you worked with her on. Could you tell me a little bit about that?

Well, she liked for things to be just about so and sound very good to my ears. And if you were one of the musicians, why -- and you didn't sound good to her, she would let you know. So -- because she had the sound of the blues (inaudible) and she liked (inaudible). That's about the whole thing.

Right. Right. Do you -- do you know why some people didn't get quite as much? Like Edith Wilson didn't get, you know, quite as much of the breaks maybe as some of the others in at least -- at least according to the history books?
Well, I think that was all due to the era in which they came along and who's writing. (Inaudible) who's writing or -- that's all.
